turnPublicationBoundary.source: 0x82D24EB8 loads r8 from the accepted current-turn word 0x8312B8DC. The unconditional branch at 0x82D24EC8 bypasses the two stores at 0x82D24ECC/0x82D24ED0. Branches at 0x82D24EE0 and 0x82D24EFC can return to 0x82D24AA8 and 0x82D24A90, outside this read set. Only their untaken fallthrough closes the uninterrupted source-to-local-boundary path. Alternatively the local result may be stated for a supplied r8 at 0x82D24F20 without assigning its upstream source.
turnPublicationBoundary.threshold: 0x82D24F20 reloads a pointer from stack +0x68; 0x82D24F24 reads its halfword +0x3E and 0x82D24F28 sign-extends it into r10. Let H be this signed executed value. H=0 branches at 0x82D24F30 to 0x82D24F5C; H<=-4000 branches there at 0x82D24F38. Record identity and the halfword's broader meaning are unassigned.
turnPublicationBoundary.helperEffects: The direct call at 0x82D24F48 targets accepted TurnToYear 0x82CEFA20 and returns to 0x82D24F4C. Its complete 0x82CEFA20..0x82CEFA9C body has no memory access, outgoing call or CTR write. It changes only GPR r3/r11 plus CR6, CR0 and XER carry state, preserving caller r8, r9, r10 and r18. Its early signed-nonpositive-input return and counted positive-input path both satisfy that effect bound. Reuse RVA-SYM-0219's calendar formula; this result does not redefine it.
turnPublicationBoundary.incrementArm: For H!=0 and H>-4000, 0x82D24F40 increments retained r8, 0x82D24F44 passes it in r3, and 0x82D24F48 calls TurnToYear. 0x82D24F4C stores the returned low32 calendar value at 0x8312B8E0. The fresh signed comparison at 0x82D24F50 branches at 0x82D24F54 back to the increment while returned year < H. Thus this arm may perform multiple increments. On a finite normal exit it writes final r8 low32 to current-turn word 0x8312B8DC at 0x82D24F58.
turnPublicationBoundary.bypassArm: H=0 or H<=-4000 bypasses the increment loop and the selected calendar-value/current-turn stores at 0x82D24F4C/0x82D24F58. It still reaches scheduling publication with unchanged local r8. Equality with the current-turn word on this arm requires that incoming r8 low32 equals that word and remains valid through this local interval; the no-backedge fallthrough from 0x82D24EB8 supplies one conditional source join.
turnPublicationBoundary.storesAndAliases: 0x82D24F64 loads destination P from stack +0x58. 0x82D24F70 stores r8 low32 at P before 0x82D24F74 stores the same r8 low32 at 0x8312B8D8. No instruction between 0x82D24F58 and 0x82D24F74 writes r8. destinationProducerBoundary supplies a checked constant-source alternative, not unconditional source retention. To retain current-turn equality, require the P store to preserve bytes [0x8312B8DC,0x8312B8E0): sufficient cases are a disjoint four-byte destination or P=0x8312B8DC, which writes the same full word. An unchecked P can still partially overlap.
